title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from this and the neighbouring pages). M is a profinite group of 'modular' type, plausibly a profinite completion related to GL(2,Z) or to the automorphisms of the profinite fundamental group of a once-punctured elliptic curve; the identification is not certain. Π_0 is a normal (profinite, free-like) subgroup and μ = {±1}. M^! = M^!_0 × μ, with M^!_0 ≅ \hat Π_Q · π_0. ε_2 : M → μ is a character, and σ is an involution satisfying (40): σ(x) ≡ ε_2(x)·x mod Π_0. ρ is a torsion element (order 3 or 6), with centralizer Z_ρ and normalizer N^*_ρ = μ_{τ'}·Z_ρ. τ ∈ M(σ) ⊂ M^!_0 and τ' = τσ.

Inside Z_ρ there are four subgroups (39):
- Z^!_ρ = Z_ρ ∩ M^! = M'(-j) × μ;
- Z^!_{ρ0} = Z_ρ ∩ M^!_0 = M'(-j);
- M^0(-j) = Z_ρ ∩ M''^!_0;
- M^0(-j) × μ.
The previous page showed all four are normal in Z_ρ. The problem is which of them are normal in N^*_ρ, i.e. which are normalized by τ'.

Computation on this page.
1. τ lies in M^!_0, so it acts on M^! = M^!_0 × μ by inner conjugation on the first factor and trivially on μ.
2. Since τ' = τσ, (40) gives (41): τ'(x) ≡ ε_2(x)·τ(x) mod Π_0 for x ∈ M.
3. For x ∈ M^!_0, τ(x) ∈ M^!_0 and Π_0 ⊂ M^!_0. Because the product M^!_0 × μ is direct, this gives (42): τ'(x) ∈ M^!_0 ⇔ ε_2(x) = 1. In particular M''^!_0 = M''(0)·Π_0, on which ε_2 is presumably trivial, is stable.
4. τ' normalizes Z_ρ and Z^!_ρ. Intersecting with Z_ρ gives (43): for x ∈ M'(-j), τ'(x) ∈ M'(-j) ⇔ ε_2(x) = 1.

Corollaries.
- M'(-j) is not normalized by τ', hence is not normal in N_ρ. This tacitly uses that ε_2 is nontrivial on M'(-j).
- M^0(-j) = Z_ρ ∩ M''^!_0 is normalized by τ', and so is M^0(-j) × μ.
- Conclusion: of the four subgroups (39), only M'(-j) = Z^!_{ρ0} fails to be normal in N_ρ.

The next page continues: the smallest one, M^0(-J), has index 24 in N^*_ρ. The quotient of order 24 contains D_ρ ≅ D_6 (order 12), the normalizer of L_ρ in GL(2,Z), as an index-2 subgroup, mirroring D_ρ ⊂ 𝔊/Π_0.

Purpose: a fine structural analysis of the normalizer of a torsion element (elliptic point of order 3/6) in a profinite modular-type group. This is part of the 'équation des lacets' study of Galois/GT-type actions, through rigidity of finite subgroups and their normalizers.
errors: Statement (42) as written ('τ'(x) ≡ x (Π_0)') is stronger than what (41) yields. (41) gives τ'(x) ≡ ε_2(x)τ(x) mod Π_0, and τ(x) ≡ x mod Π_0 requires an extra fact, e.g. that M^!_0/Π_0 is abelian or that τ ∈ Π_0-coset centralizing. The intended equivalence, τ'(x) ∈ M^!_0 ⇔ ε_2(x) = 1, is correct.
'en particulier, M''^!_0 est normalisé par τ' should presumably read τ'. For τ itself the statement is trivial or already known from Cor. 2 of the previous page.
The corollary that M'(-j) is not normalized by τ' tacitly assumes ε_2 is nontrivial on M'(-j); this is not verified on the page.

ideas.what: Determination of which natural subgroups of the centralizer Z_ρ of a torsion element are normal in its normalizer, via a sign character ε_2 twisting conjugation by an involution σ
ideas.modern_name: Normalizers/centralizers of finite-order elements in profinite completions of GL(2,Z) / Out(\hat F_2); local structure at elliptic points in Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type settings
ideas.usually_credited_to: Background: Grothendieck's Esquisse (1984); later Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura on GT and finite subgroups. The specific computation is not attested.
ideas.where_published: Themes in Esquisse d'un programme / La Longue Marche; this specific computation is not known to be published

deep.surprise_reason: A routine group-theoretic bookkeeping step: which subgroups are normalized by τ' = τσ, using a sign character. It is internally consistent and of interest only as part of Grothendieck's detailed study of normalizers of torsion elements; there is no new concept or uncredited result on this page.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 reads 'τ ∈ M(σ) ⊂ M^!_0 normalise M^!_0, donc il opère sur M^! = M^!_0 × μ par l'opération produit...'; the struck-out letter is a stray 'Z'.
In (42) the marginal insertion reads '(Π_0), ⟺ τ'(x) ∈ M^!_0' placed above 'τ'(x) ≡ x ⟺ ε_2(x)=1'.
'normalisé dans Z^*_ρ' in the Corollaire is likely 'invariant/normal dans N^*_ρ'; the handwriting is a corrected 'N_ρ^*'.
'normalisé par τ', donc aussi son produit par μ' ('donc aussi par produit par μ' in the transcription).
